title: Deducting an outstanding no-show charge from a class-credit pack refund
content:
## Scope
This document covers the Group Fitness Class Passes product line. It states how an outstanding no-show charge already on a pack's history reduces the refund figure before that refund is finalized.

## Applicable condition
Where this pack's history already carries a no-show fee charge that has not yet been offset elsewhere, that amount is subtracted once from the refund figure before it is finalized, with the subtraction never carrying the result past zero. Where this pack's history carries no such unoffset charge, no subtraction is made and the refund figure reached so far carries forward unchanged.

## Basis
Before this pack's refund is finalized, the amount of any such fee charge already logged against the pack's history that has not yet been offset elsewhere is subtracted once from the refund figure reached at that point. The floor of zero applies to this subtraction: where the outstanding charge would otherwise carry the figure below zero, the subtraction stops at zero instead.

## Frequently confirmed points
Q: What if the pack's history carries two separate no-show charges, neither yet offset?
A: Both are counted toward the single deduction; the subtraction is applied once, using their combined amount.
Q: Can this subtraction ever produce a negative refund figure?
A: No — the floor of zero always stops the subtraction at zero rather than going negative.

## Hypothetical worked example (illustration only)
Suppose, purely for illustration, the refund figure reached before this step were $30.00, and an unoffset no-show charge of $25.00 already sat on the pack's history. The subtraction leaves $5.00. Had the unoffset charge instead been $40.00, the subtraction would stop at zero rather than produce a negative figure.
